issues.t: Active Body Control (ABC) suspension leaks and sagging
issues.sym: A corner of the car sinks after it sits for a day or two, an ABC warning appears, the ride turns bouncy or harsh, or you hear a hum from the engine bay at low revs. Red hydraulic fluid may drip under the car.
issues.why: ABC is a high-pressure hydraulic suspension. With age its hoses, seals and struts leak, the gas-filled accumulators lose their charge, the pulsation damper fails, and dirty or low fluid wears the pump.
issues.next: If the car drops low or shows a red ABC warning, stop and don't drive it. Have a specialist check fluid level and pressure and find the leak. Regular fluid and filter changes help prevent failures.

issues.sym: A brake warning message on the dash, the brake pump buzzing often, or a hard pedal with less braking help. Some owners say the pedal feels soft or sinks.
issues.why: These cars use an electro-hydraulic brake system (Sensotronic Brake Control). Its pump unit is designed for a set number of brake cycles and then needs replacing; some fail early.
issues.next: Treat any brake warning seriously and get the car checked before driving far. Ask a dealer whether your car is still covered: Mercedes extended coverage on this unit to 25 years with unlimited miles.

issues.t: Electronic brake system can switch to backup mode (recall)
issues.sym: A brake malfunction warning and a hard pedal that needs much more force to stop the car.
issues.why: A fault in the SBC hydraulic unit or its pump ground wire can make the system fall back to its backup mode, which has much less brake assist. Mercedes recalled the cars (04V-296 and 05V-133).
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the free dealer repair done if it was never completed.

issues.t: ABC front sensors can give wrong readings (recall)
issues.sym: An ABC warning message, body lean or an uneven ride height.
issues.why: Solder joints on the front acceleration sensor circuit boards could fail, so the suspension computer gets false readings. Mercedes recalled affected cars (08V-405).
issues.next: Check for an open recall with your VIN; the dealer replaces the sensors for free.

issues.t: Folding hardtop (Vario roof) hydraulic leaks or slow operation
issues.sym: The roof works slowly, stops partway, or won't open; you may see hydraulic fluid on the headliner or in the trunk, wet footwells, rattles or wind noise.
issues.why: The roof's hydraulic rams lose their seals with age, often starting with the front roof latch cylinder. A weak battery or flaps at the rear deck that aren't fully closed can also stop the roof.
issues.next: Charge or test the battery first, then have a specialist check fluid level and look for leaking rams. Rebuilt rams and seal kits cost much less than new dealer parts.

issues.t: Balance shaft or idler gear wear on V8 (P0016/P0017)
issues.sym: Check engine light with codes P0016 or P0017, later followed by a timing chain rattle.
issues.why: On some early 5.5L V8 engines, the idler gear in the timing drive was made of a metal that wears too fast. The chain gets slack and the cam timing drifts; in the worst case valves can hit pistons.
issues.next: Don't ignore these codes. Have the timing checked by a Mercedes specialist, and ask whether your engine serial number has the updated gear.

issues.sym: Loss of power, poorer fuel economy, rough idle and a check engine light.
issues.why: Oily carbon from the crankcase ventilation system builds up in the intake manifold, and its plastic flaps and linkages get brittle and break.
issues.next: Have the codes read. The manifold can be replaced or, in some cases, repaired with a kit.

issues.sym: Coolant level drops while the oil level rises, white smoke, rough idle and eventually sludgy oil.
issues.why: Head bolts on earlier 6.2L AMG engines can corrode and lose clamping force, letting coolant leak into the cylinders or oil. Mercedes changed the bolts in mid-2010.
issues.next: Stop driving if coolant is disappearing or the oil looks milky, since this can wreck the engine. Have a cooling system pressure test and oil check done.

issues.sym: A ticking noise from the top of the engine on cold starts that slowly gets more persistent.
issues.why: On the 6.2L AMG V8 the camshaft lobes can wear against the harder cam followers.
issues.next: Have a specialist inspect the camshafts, ideally before buying. Keep up regular oil changes with the correct oil.

issues.sym: Misfiring, shaking, loss of power and a flashing check engine light.
issues.why: The V12 uses two large coil packs, each serving six cylinders, and they fail often. The 24 spark plugs also need regular replacement.
issues.next: Have the misfire codes read. If a coil pack has failed, ask for the updated part and check when the spark plugs were last done.

issues.sym: Clunks when shifting or accelerating and more vibration in the cabin.
issues.why: The twin-turbo V12's high torque wears out its fluid-filled engine mounts, roughly every 40,000 miles. Other R230 engines also wear their mounts, just more slowly.
issues.next: Have the mounts checked if you notice clunking. On V12 cars the job is big, so get a quote from a specialist first.

issues.t: Shift lever breaks and leaves car stuck in Park
issues.sym: The gear selector won't move out of Park or feels loose.
issues.why: A plastic part inside the shifter mechanism wears out and breaks.
issues.next: A shop or skilled owner can fit a stronger metal replacement part. It's worth doing early.

issues.t: Transmission fluid leaking through electrical plug
issues.sym: Fluid seeping where the wiring plug enters the transmission, then harsh shifts, a stuck gear or no gear selection.
issues.why: The seal on the transmission's electrical connector ages and lets fluid wick up the wiring toward the transmission control unit.
issues.next: Have the connector seal replaced as soon as you see seepage; it is a cheap fix. Waiting can damage the control unit, which is expensive.

issues.t: Fuel smell in the cabin (early cars)
issues.sym: A fuel smell inside, especially after idling for 10 minutes or more with the top up.
issues.why: Early cars had fuel tank problems; owners also mention a loose baffle plate inside the tank on 2003-2004 models.
issues.next: Have the smell checked promptly for leaks, since fuel vapor is a fire risk.

issues.sym: Water in the trunk after rain or a car wash, sometimes with rust under the seal.
issues.why: The rubber seal along the top of the trunk lets water in after several years.
issues.next: Clean out any rust and refit the seal with proper sealant; just replacing the rubber may not stop it.

issues.sym: Puddles of hydraulic fluid near the rear wheels, drips behind the sun visors, or a top that is slow or won't close.
issues.why: The soft top is moved by about a dozen hydraulic cylinders whose seals leak with age. Low fluid in the reservoir under the spare wheel makes the top reluctant to close.
issues.next: Check the fluid level first, then find which cylinders leak. Rebuilt or aftermarket cylinders cost far less than dealer parts.

issues.t: Soft top stops working (roof control module)
issues.sym: The top won't open or close at all, or stops partway.
issues.why: The roof control module under the rear seat can fail, and it can be damaged by a voltage spike during a jump-start. Worn sensors and micro switches also stop the sequence.
issues.next: Have the roof system scanned before replacing parts. Be careful when jump-starting these cars.

issues.sym: Oil or coolant seeping at the front or rear of the cylinder head, coolant loss, or overheating.
issues.why: The 3.2L six-cylinder engine is known for head gasket leaks.
issues.next: Watch coolant and oil levels and have a leak check done. Fix it before the engine overheats.

issues.t: Tappet noise from oil feed tubes (early SL500)
issues.sym: A ticking, "tappety" noise from the top of the engine.
issues.why: Plastic oil supply tubes to the valve lifters on the early 32-valve V8 lose pressure, starving the lifters of oil so they wear.
issues.next: Have it checked soon. Later metal tubes last longer; worn lifters may need replacing too.

issues.t: Front ball joints and strut mounts wearing
issues.sym: Creaking or clunking from the front over bumps, vague steering or uneven tire wear.
issues.why: The heavy V8 and V12 cars wear the front lower ball joints and the top strut mounts, and the rubber mounts can crack.
issues.next: Have the front suspension inspected and replace worn parts in pairs, then get an alignment.

issues.sym: A metallic rattle from under the car at idle and possibly a check engine light.
issues.why: The inside of the catalytic converter breaks up with age.
issues.next: Have a shop confirm the source of the rattle. Replacement is one of the more expensive repairs on these cars.

issues.t: Rust in wheel arches, lower wings and trunk floor
issues.sym: Bubbling paint at the wheel arches, lower front wings near the bumper, bottom of the hardtop pillars, or water and rust in the trunk floor.
issues.why: Debris collects in these areas and holds moisture; water can also enter the trunk through the high-mounted brake light and old hardtop seals.
issues.next: Clean out drain areas, check the trunk floor under the mat, and have rust treated early before it spreads.

issues.t: Rusty brake lines over rear subframe
issues.sym: A soft brake pedal, a brake fluid leak or visible corrosion on brake pipes.
issues.why: Brake pipes rust where they pass over the rear subframe and the rubber hoses perish with age.
issues.next: Have the brake lines inspected at every service. Replacing the rear lines is labor-heavy because the subframe has to come down.

issues.sym: Check engine light, sometimes with rough running or oil seeping around the round solenoids on the front of the engine.
issues.why: The electric solenoids that control variable valve timing fail with age and can let oil into their connectors.
issues.next: Have the codes read. The solenoids are fairly cheap; check the wiring plugs for oil while the job is done.

issues.sym: Check engine light, possibly with a sulfur smell or reduced power.
issues.why: Mercedes issued an extended warranty for the catalytic converters on the 4.7L twin-turbo V8.
issues.next: Ask a Mercedes dealer whether your car is still covered under the extended catalytic converter warranty before paying for a repair.

issues.sym: A coolant warning on the dash, a sweet smell, or coolant under the car. One owner was stranded when a radiator hose came loose.
issues.why: Mercedes issued a service bulletin for coolant warnings caused by a leaking coolant line, and hoses can come loose.
issues.next: Don't keep driving with a coolant warning. Check the level when the engine is cold and have the leak found.

issues.sym: A message about the auxiliary battery or start/stop not working.
issues.why: These cars have a small second battery that supports electronics; it wears out after several years.
issues.next: Have the auxiliary battery tested and replaced; it's a routine job.

issues.sym: A humming or droning noise from the engine bay at low revs, or ABC warnings, on cars with Active Body Control.
issues.why: The pulsation damper that smooths pressure from the ABC pump fails and can leak.
issues.next: Have the ABC system checked by a specialist; a CPO or extended warranty may cover it.

issues.t: Steering column noise or height adjustment jamming
issues.sym: Grinding or creaking from the steering column, or the power column getting stuck at its top or bottom position.
issues.why: Mercedes issued service bulletins for noises in the steering column area and jamming of the height adjustment.
issues.next: Mention the bulletins to the dealer; they describe the fix.

issues.sym: The engine may stop while driving and lose drive power.
issues.why: The fuel pump can shut down. Mercedes recalled many models including the SL (23V-445, expanded by 23V-880).
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall; the dealer replaces the fuel pump for free.

issues.sym: Sudden loss of drive power with no warning, or a burning smell.
issues.why: The starter/alternator wiring harness may not be secured and can rub on the drive shaft, causing a short circuit (23V-676).
issues.next: Check for an open recall; the dealer secures the harness for free.

issues.sym: Sudden loss of drive power, or safety systems and the instrument cluster switching off.
issues.why: Some 80-amp fuses were made incorrectly and can fail; Mercedes replaced the main fuse boxes (24V-115).
issues.next: Check for an open recall; the dealer replaces the fuse boxes for free.

issues.t: Wrong fuse box fitted during earlier recall (recall)
issues.sym: Possible sudden loss of drive power or safety functions, and a higher fire risk.
issues.why: Some cars repaired under the earlier fuse recall received a fuse box not meant for the car (25V-255).
issues.next: Even if the first fuse recall was done, check your VIN again; the dealer inspects and replaces the fuse boxes for free.

issues.t: Hands-off-wheel warning may not work with DISTRONIC (recall)
issues.sym: When using adaptive cruise with steering assist, the car may not warn you that your hands are off the wheel.
issues.why: A software error in the steering wheel hand-detection unit (22V-189).
issues.next: Have the free software update done at a dealer, and keep your hands on the wheel.

issues.sym: Usually nothing noticeable at first; corrosion may be found on the body near the headlamp housing.
issues.why: Mercedes issued a service bulletin saying certain bolts on the headlamp housing can cause corrosion on the body.
issues.next: Ask the dealer to check this bulletin; repairs should be covered while the car is under warranty.
